PharmaErp modernisation: legacy vs migrated parity report

Java 8 servlets/JSP/Hibernate 5.2 → Java 21 · Spring Boot 3.3.13 · React 18 · MySQL 8 · Docker Compose  |  commit ccfaa56ad3f8  |  generated 2026-10-23 19:24 UTC

1. Executive summary

No regressions observed. Both estates were started side by side from the same seed data and the 16 recorded legacy behaviours were replayed against each. 6 behave identically, 10 differ on purpose (2 legacy defect fixes, 8 modernisation changes, each with a documented root cause) and 0 are regressions. After the replay both databases hold the same users and students, and every user still signs in with the same password; the migrated estate now stores those passwords as BCrypt hashes instead of plaintext.

The legacy codebase has no automated tests (0, recorded from ./gradlew test under JDK 8). The migrated estate runs 360 backend tests (360 passed, 0 failed) and 121 frontend tests (121 passed, 0 failed). Two legacy security defects observed in the baseline are closed: an unauthenticated endpoint that issued an admin token (F15) and an HQL injection point that leaked internal exceptions (F10).

2. Scope: what was compared and what was built net-new

Legacy actually implemented (compared here)

  • Login: GET/POST /login (fields email, password), plaintext compare after trimming the username, RS256 JWT in the body plus a token cookie
  • GET /token (mints an admin JWT for hard-coded tarangparikh)
  • GET / → 302 /redirect (JSP login page)
  • Tables user and student; username/password validation rules

Specification only in legacy (built net-new)

  • Staff, stores, clients, manufacturers
  • Inventory, stock status, tracking, expiry
  • Finance, invoices, GST
  • Payments, feedback

Source: ERP-Pharma Excel Sheets.xlsx and Pharma ERP USE-CASE.pdf. These modules had no legacy code, so there is nothing to compare them against. The evidence for them is the migrated test suites (§5) and the screenshots (§9).

How parity was measured

  • 16 recorded HTTP flows (parity/flows.json) replayed with parity/capture.py; the migrated run targeted the backend's legacy-compat routes
  • Flow-by-flow classification by parity/diff.py against parity/known-differences.json: a change counts as intentional only if the migrated response matches the documented expectation exactly. Anything else is a regression.
  • Database state compared by parity/datastate.py

Global non-functional differences (every flow; these do not affect the classification above)

  • cookie.JSESSIONID (modernisation): Legacy Tomcat creates an HTTP session (JSESSIONID) on JSP/servlet requests. The migrated API is stateless (SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS); the only auth state is the JWT 'token' cookie / Bearer header.
  • jwt.signature_len (modernisation): Legacy signs with the RSA-1024 private key committed to the repo (WEB-INF/StoredObject/system.key; 171-char RS256 signature). Migrated generates a per-environment RSA-2048 key pair at first start (jwt-keys service; 342-char signature). Algorithm (RS256), claims and TTL are unchanged; tokens are not interchangeable between the estates.

Regressions

  • None observed.

7. Every difference, with its root cause

F01 Root redirects to login page (modernisation)

FieldLegacyMigrated
content_type"text/html"null
location"/redirect""/signin"

Root cause. GET / still answers 302, but the target is the SPA sign-in route /signin instead of the JSP /redirect page. Same user outcome: an anonymous visitor lands on the login form.

F02 Login page renders (modernisation)

FieldLegacyMigrated
body_kind"html-login-page""empty"
content_type"text/html"null
locationnull"/signin"
status200302

Root cause. The JSP login page was replaced by the React SPA. The backend keeps /redirect as a legacy-compat route that 302s to the SPA sign-in page (/signin), which the nginx front door serves with 200 (verified by parity/probes.sh).

F05 Login wrong password (modernisation)

FieldLegacyMigrated
body_kind"html-login-page""empty"
content_type"text/html"null
locationnull"/signin?error"
status200302

Root cause. Legacy forwarded a failed login to the JSP login page (200). Migrated uses Post/Redirect/Get: 302 to /signin?error. Same outcome: no token, no cookie, back on the login form. Known limitation: the React sign-in page does not read ?error yet, so a failed legacy-style form POST shows the empty form without an error banner (the SPA's own JSON sign-in does show one).

F06 Login unknown user (modernisation)

FieldLegacyMigrated
body_kind"html-login-page""empty"
content_type"text/html"null
locationnull"/signin?error"
status200302

Root cause. Same Post/Redirect/Get change as F05. Unknown users and wrong passwords stay indistinguishable (same redirect; AuthService burns one BCrypt check for unknown users so timing does not leak either).

F07 Login with no parameters (modernisation)

FieldLegacyMigrated
body_kind"html-login-page""empty"
content_type"text/html"null
locationnull"/signin"
status200302

Root cause. Legacy silently fell through to the login page when email/password were missing. Migrated redirects to /signin without ?error (nothing was attempted). No token, no cookie.

F09 Password comparison is case-sensitive (modernisation)

FieldLegacyMigrated
body_kind"html-login-page""empty"
content_type"text/html"null
locationnull"/signin?error"
status200302

Root cause. Password comparison is still case-sensitive (PARISDKH rejected); only the failure transport changed (Post/Redirect/Get, see F05).

F10 Username containing a quote (HQL injection probe) (defect fix)

FieldLegacyMigrated
body_kind"error-text-leak""empty"
locationnull"/signin?error"
status200302

Root cause. Legacy built HQL by string concatenation (FROM com.schema.User U WHERE U.username='...'), so a quote produced org.hibernate.QueryException and the exception text was returned to the client (injection surface + information leak). Migrated looks the user up by primary key through Spring Data JPA (bound parameter) and treats it as an ordinary failed login.

F11 Classic injection payload does not bypass auth (modernisation)

FieldLegacyMigrated
body_kind"html-login-page""empty"
content_type"text/html"null
locationnull"/signin?error"
status200302

Root cause. Injection payload is rejected on both sides (legacy happened to fail the plaintext compare). Migrated uses a bound parameter and the Post/Redirect/Get failure transport (see F05).

F15 Unauthenticated GET /token (defect fix)

FieldLegacyMigrated
body_jwt{"alg": "RS256", "claims": {"scope": "admin", "sub": "user/login", "username": "tarangparikh"}, "ttl_seconds_approx": 3600, "valid_shape": true}null
body_kind"json-jwt-string""json"
body_valuenull{"detail": "Authentication required", "instance": "/token", "status": 401, "title": "Unauthorized", "type": "about:blank"}
content_type"application/json""application/problem+json"
status200401
token_cookie{"alg": "RS256", "claims": {"scope": "admin", "sub": "user/login", "username": "tarangparikh"}, "ttl_seconds_approx": 3600, "valid_shape": true}null

Root cause. Legacy GET /token minted a signed admin JWT for the hard-coded user 'tarangparikh' to any unauthenticated caller (privilege-escalation defect). Migrated /token only re-issues a token for a caller that already presents a valid JWT (cookie or Bearer) and returns RFC 7807 401 otherwise.

F16 Unknown route returns 404 (modernisation)

FieldLegacyMigrated
body_kind"other""json"
body_valuenull{"detail": "Authentication required", "instance": "/nonexistent", "status": 401, "title": "Unauthorized", "type": "about:blank"}
content_type"text/html""application/problem+json"
status404401

Root cause. Spring Security is deny-by-default: unauthenticated requests to any non-public path get 401 before routing, so anonymous callers cannot enumerate routes. An authenticated request to /nonexistent returns 404 (verified by parity/probes.sh), and the nginx front door serves the SPA for unknown browser routes.

8. Verified parity, known limitations, pre-existing legacy defects

Verified parity (observed identical)

  • F03 Login success (form POST) returns JWT body + token cookie: 200 · json-jwt-string · JWT RS256 username=tarang scope=admin · token cookie set
  • F04 Login success via GET query string: 200 · json-jwt-string · JWT RS256 username=tarang scope=admin · token cookie set
  • F08 Login username padded with whitespace is trimmed: 200 · json-jwt-string · JWT RS256 username=tarang scope=admin · token cookie set
  • F12 Login seeded user pharmacist01: 200 · json-jwt-string · JWT RS256 username=pharmacist01 scope=admin · token cookie set
  • F13 Login seeded user storemgr: 200 · json-jwt-string · JWT RS256 username=storemgr scope=admin · token cookie set
  • F14 Login seeded user accounts: 200 · json-jwt-string · JWT RS256 username=accounts scope=admin · token cookie set
  • Same JWT contract on success: RS256, sub=user/login, username, scope=admin, 1 h TTL, token cookie
  • Same users after replay, all signing in with the same passwords (§6)

Known limitations of the migrated estate

  • A failed legacy-style form login lands on /signin?error, but the React sign-in page does not read ?error, so no error banner is shown. The SPA's own sign-in does show one. See the screenshot in §9.
  • Legacy and migrated JWTs are not interchangeable (different keys): a legacy-minted token gets 401 from the migrated API (see parity/results/probes.txt). Active legacy sessions must sign in again after cutover.
  • The student table is empty in the seed on both sides, so the parity run compares only its row count and schema presence. No legacy code path writes to it.
  • The net-new modules (§2) have no legacy baseline. Their evidence is the migrated tests and screenshots, not parity.
  • Each parity run needs fresh volumes (docker compose down -v), because load-seed.sh refuses to load into a non-empty user table.

Pre-existing legacy defects (observed in the legacy estate)

  • F15: GET /token returns a signed admin JWT for hard-coded tarangparikh to any unauthenticated caller. Fixed (401 without a valid token).
  • F10: a quote in the username yields an org.hibernate.QueryException text response (HQL built by string concatenation). Fixed (bound parameters, ordinary failed login).
  • Passwords stored and compared in plaintext. Fixed (BCrypt, upgraded on sign-in).
  • RSA-1024 signing key committed to the repo (WEB-INF/StoredObject/system.key). Fixed (a per-environment RSA-2048 key is generated at first start).
  • The JSP login page shows both "Error" callouts on first load, before any submission (legacy login screenshot, §9).
  • F07: missing parameters fall through to the login page without feedback.

10. Supplementary probes (parity/probes.sh)

These check the parts of the migrated behaviour that the 16-flow replay cannot reach: the browser front door, authenticated /token reissue, and cross-estate token rejection. Each probe asserts an expected result (OK/FAIL), and the script exits 1 on any FAIL.

# legacy-compat routes
OK   F02 front door GET /redirect (follow redirects)                -> 200 http://127.0.0.1:8080/signin
OK   F01 front door GET / (SPA)                                     -> 200 text/html
OK   F16 backend GET /nonexistent with Bearer token                 -> 404
OK   F16 front door GET /nonexistent (SPA fallback)                 -> 200 text/html
OK   F15 backend GET /token with token cookie                       -> 200 application/json
OK   F15 backend GET /token with Bearer token                       -> 200 application/json
OK   F15 backend GET /token with forged/garbage token               -> 401
OK   F15 legacy GET /token, no credentials (legacy defect)          -> 200 application/json;charset=ISO-8859-1
# cross-estate tokens
OK   legacy-minted 'tarangparikh' JWT presented to migrated /api/auth/me -> 401
OK   migrated JWT presented to migrated /api/auth/me                -> 200
# result: all probes met their expected result

11. How to reproduce

git checkout devin/hcl-t13-parity
# legacy estate (Tomcat 9 / JDK 8 / MySQL 5.7, port 8081), seeded from parity/seed/
docker compose -f parity/legacy/docker-compose.yml up -d --build --wait
# migrated estate (MySQL 8 / Spring Boot backend 8090 / nginx+React 8080), then the identical seed users
docker compose up -d --build --wait
parity/migrated/load-seed.sh
# replay and classify
python3 parity/capture.py --base http://127.0.0.1:8081 --label legacy   --out parity/results/legacy.json
python3 parity/capture.py --base http://127.0.0.1:8090 --label migrated --out parity/results/migrated.json
python3 parity/diff.py                       # -> parity/results/diff.json (exit 1 on any REGRESSION)
python3 parity/datastate.py --out parity/results/data-state.json   # needs pip bcrypt
parity/probes.sh > parity/results/probes.txt
python3 parity/screenshots.py                # -> parity/report/screenshots/ (needs playwright)
python3 parity/environment.py > parity/results/environment.json
# test suites
(JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-8-openjdk-amd64 ./gradlew test)               # legacy: 0 tests
(cd backend && JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64 ./gradlew test)
(cd frontend && npm ci && npx vitest run)
python3 parity/report/build_report.py        # -> parity/report/pharmaerp-parity-report.html
# reset for another run
docker compose down -v; docker compose -f parity/legacy/docker-compose.yml down -v
